cb-001.concept: A diode conducts mainly in one direction. Rectifier, signal and Schottky types serve different jobs.
cb-001.check: Select the exact diode number, current rating and reverse-voltage rating; do not treat all listed types as substitutes.

cb-002.concept: Resistance limits current and divides voltage. Use Ohm’s law to select a value before connecting an LED.
cb-002.check: Choose the required resistance, tolerance and power rating. R = (supply voltage − LED forward voltage) / target current.
specs: ¼ W metal film; select value

cb-003.concept: A capacitor stores charge. Its value, working voltage and polarity determine where it can be used.
cb-003.check: Electrolytic types are polarized. Use a voltage rating above the circuit voltage and discharge before rewiring.

cb-018.concept: A Bluetooth serial module bridges UART data to a compatible Bluetooth Classic serial connection.
cb-018.check: Breakout supply tolerance is not UART input tolerance. Confirm level shifting and host support; do not apply 5 V directly to an unprotected RX pin.

cb-019.concept: A small OLED displays pixels rather than fixed character cells.
cb-019.check: Check SSD1306 versus other controllers, I²C address and pull-up voltage before using a library.

cb-022.check: Verify pin labels, output polarity and required voltage. Reflective detection distance depends strongly on the target.

cb-024.check: This is an educational sensor, not a certified fire alarm. Do not test with an uncontrolled flame or rely on it for life safety.

cb-025.concept: A Hall sensor responds to magnetic fields; linear and switching variants behave differently.
cb-025.check: Identify linear, latch or switch type, required magnet polarity, supply and output circuit. NJK-5002C is a magnetic proximity device, not a general metal detector.

cb-051.concept: A Hall sensor responds to magnetic fields; linear and switching variants behave differently.
cb-051.check: Identify linear, latch or switch type, required magnet polarity, supply and output circuit. NJK-5002C is a magnetic proximity device, not a general metal detector.

cb-026.concept: A touch module detects an electrical change when a conductive surface is touched.
cb-026.check: Keep accessible surfaces at extra-low voltage and check sensitivity and output polarity.

cb-027.concept: A thermistor changes resistance with temperature; a comparator may add an adjustable threshold.
cb-027.check: These modules do not automatically provide calibrated degrees Celsius. Identify the thermistor and divider before applying a conversion equation.

cb-054.concept: A thermistor changes resistance with temperature; a comparator may add an adjustable threshold.
cb-054.check: These modules do not automatically provide calibrated degrees Celsius. Identify the thermistor and divider before applying a conversion equation.

cb-028.concept: An active buzzer contains an oscillator and sounds when enabled.
cb-028.check: Check whether it is a driven module or bare buzzer, its current and trigger polarity. A GPIO is a signal source, not a general power supply.

cb-029.concept: A passive piezo needs an alternating drive signal; changing frequency changes pitch.
cb-029.check: Confirm piezo versus magnetic buzzer and input current. Use a driver if the GPIO cannot safely supply the load.

cb-030.concept: A GNSS receiver estimates position from satellite signals and commonly outputs NMEA sentences.
cb-030.check: Confirm the exact module and antenna connection; the no-antenna listing needs a compatible antenna. TTL UART is not ±RS232. Test outdoors with clear sky.

cb-083.concept: A GNSS receiver estimates position from satellite signals and commonly outputs NMEA sentences.
cb-083.check: Confirm the exact module and antenna connection; the no-antenna listing needs a compatible antenna. TTL UART is not ±RS232. Test outdoors with clear sky.

cb-031.concept: A battery clip connects a rectangular 9 V battery to a barrel plug.
cb-031.check: Confirm polarity. A small rectangular 9 V battery is unsuitable for modem surges, motors or long runtime.

cb-032.concept: A switching converter trades voltage and current while regulating its output. Boost raises voltage; buck lowers it.
cb-032.check: Check input range, topology, output setting and thermal capacity. Advertised switch current is not guaranteed continuous output current. Measure the output before connecting electronics.

cb-069.check: Check input range, topology, output setting and thermal capacity. Advertised switch current is not guaranteed continuous output current. Measure the output before connecting electronics.

cb-075.check: Check input range, topology, output setting and thermal capacity. Advertised switch current is not guaranteed continuous output current. Measure the output before connecting electronics.

cb-033.check: Confirm chemistry, protection circuit and cell rating. This is not automatically a load-sharing UPS; a connected load can interfere with charge termination.

cb-038.concept: A magnetic field changes a reed contact. It can indicate whether a magnet remains near a door or lid.
cb-038.check: Confirm module pinout and signal polarity with Serial Monitor. Use a magnet; do not infer closed/open from wire colors.
specs: Contact state depends on magnet position

cb-040.concept: An optical sensor can show small light changes associated with a pulse.
cb-040.check: Educational use only. Movement and lighting affect readings; this is not a diagnostic medical device.

cb-042.concept: A laser module emits a narrow beam that can be aimed at a detector.
cb-042.check: Confirm laser class and output power. Never aim at eyes, vehicles, aircraft or reflective surfaces; use an enclosed beam path.

cb-044.concept: A mechanical contact changes briefly during a vibration or knock.
cb-044.check: Debounce and time-filter the signal; it is not a calibrated acceleration sensor.

cb-057.concept: A mechanical contact changes briefly during a vibration or knock.
cb-057.check: Debounce and time-filter the signal; it is not a calibrated acceleration sensor.

cb-045.concept: A rotary encoder outputs phase-shifted pulses to describe incremental rotation.
cb-045.check: Debounce contacts and decode direction. Incremental counts do not provide an absolute shaft angle after power loss.

cb-046.concept: A tilt-sensitive contact changes with orientation; some listed variants contain mercury.
cb-046.check: Use the non-mercury tilt switch when possible. Never open or break a mercury-containing part; handle disposal appropriately.

cb-049.check: Output direction depends on the onboard divider. Calibrate bright and dark readings first; raw ADC counts are not lux.
specs: Measure dark and bright ADC values

cb-050.concept: A DHT sensor provides digitally encoded humidity and temperature measurements.
cb-050.check: Use the matching sensor type in code and a data pull-up to the controller supply. Allow at least 2 seconds between reads and detect invalid readings.

cb-079.concept: A DHT sensor provides digitally encoded humidity and temperature measurements.
cb-079.check: Use the matching sensor type in code and a data pull-up to the controller supply. Allow at least 2 seconds between reads and detect invalid readings.

cb-053.check: Read the package marking before selecting a library. Do not assume a DS18B20 or a particular pinout from the generic product name.

cb-055.concept: Infrared remote controls encode bursts of carrier-modulated light; a receiver demodulates compatible signals.
cb-055.check: Confirm receiver pinout and carrier frequency. A transmitter generally needs a suitable driver for useful range.

cb-059.check: Reference specifications describe an ATmega328P UNO R3. Verify the clone chip and USB interface; USB-C does not imply different logic voltage.

cb-061.concept: A GSM modem exchanges AT commands with a controller to send SMS or use legacy cellular data.
cb-061.check: SIM900A is a 2G GSM/GPRS device (900/1800 MHz), not a 3G/4G modem. Verify local 2G SMS service, kit power input and UART levels before assembly.

Bursty load; use a suitable separate supply

cb-062.concept: The ESP8266 combines a microcontroller with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. It does not include Bluetooth.
cb-062.check: NodeMCU USB power input and ADC scaling depend on the breakout. ESP8266 GPIO is not 5 V tolerant.

cb-063.concept: A classic ESP32 module combines a microcontroller with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. An expansion board exposes connections; it does not create extra independent GPIO.
cb-063.check: Verify the exact ESP32 variant and 30-pin layout. Board header labels are not sequential GPIO numbers; avoid boot-strapping pins unless their behavior is understood.
specs: 3.3 V; do not connect 5 V signals directly

cb-064.concept: A classic ESP32 module combines a microcontroller with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. An expansion board exposes connections; it does not create extra independent GPIO.

cb-066.concept: A character LCD displays two lines through an I²C backpack.
cb-066.check: Scan for the backpack address instead of assuming 0x27. Check supply, contrast and pull-up voltage when using a 3.3 V controller.

cb-067.concept: A real-time clock keeps calendar time independently of the main program.
cb-067.check: Inspect the module battery charging circuit before fitting a coin cell. Do not charge a non-rechargeable CR2032; verify the board design.

cb-068.concept: A real-time clock maintains time using a dedicated timekeeping chip and backup supply.
cb-068.check: Use a DS1302-specific library and check backup-battery/trickle-charge configuration. It is not pin-compatible with DS3231.

cb-070.concept: A hobby servo responds to repeated control pulses. Positional and continuous-rotation versions respond differently.
cb-070.check: Choose the 180° positional version for angle commands. A 360° continuous-rotation version controls speed/direction instead. Use a separate supply sized for stall current.

cb-071.concept: A hobby servo responds to repeated control pulses. Positional and continuous-rotation versions respond differently.
cb-071.check: Choose the 180° positional version for angle commands. A 360° continuous-rotation version controls speed/direction instead. Use a separate supply sized for stall current.

cb-072.concept: A stepper motor moves in increments when its coils are energized in sequence through a driver.
cb-072.check: Use the ULN2003 driver and the correct 5 V motor supply. Gear ratios and steps per revolution vary; calibrate actual movement.

cb-073.concept: An H-bridge reverses current through a motor, allowing forward/reverse control.
cb-073.check: Select the driver by motor stall current, not free-running current. Account for voltage drop and heat; L298N and L9110S ratings differ.

cb-080.concept: An H-bridge reverses current through a motor, allowing forward/reverse control.
cb-080.check: Select the driver by motor stall current, not free-running current. Account for voltage drop and heat; L298N and L9110S ratings differ.

cb-074.concept: An ultrasonic sensor measures the time taken for a sound burst to return from a target.
cb-074.check: Standard HC-SR04 uses 5 V echo. Level-shift for ESP32. Soft, angled or small targets may give no reliable echo.

cb-077.concept: A microSD adapter exposes a card through an SPI interface for removable storage.
cb-077.check: Check onboard regulation AND logic translation; a 3.3 V regulator alone does not make all SPI inputs 5 V tolerant. Use a compatible card and filesystem.

cb-081.concept: A Hall-effect current sensor produces a voltage related to the current passing through its conductor.
cb-081.check: Identify the 30 A variant and calibrate zero offset and sensitivity. Breakout trace and terminal ratings may be below the chip rating; use low-voltage DC for student work.

cb-082.concept: A resistor divider scales a measured voltage down before the ADC.
cb-082.check: A nominal 5:1 divider reaches 5 V at 25 V input and 3.3 V at 16.5 V. Stay below ADC limits with margin; verify actual divider ratio and common ground.

cb-086.concept: Soldering joins conductors; desoldering braid removes solder by capillary action.
cb-086.check: Use eye protection and fume extraction, avoid skin contact with hot tools, and wash hands after handling leaded solder.

cb-090.concept: Soldering joins conductors; desoldering braid removes solder by capillary action.
cb-090.check: Use eye protection and fume extraction, avoid skin contact with hot tools, and wash hands after handling leaded solder.

cb-091.concept: An inductive proximity sensor detects a metal target without touching it.
cb-091.check: Read the exact supply rating and NPN/PNP NO/NC wiring. Do not feed an industrial sensor supply directly into a microcontroller pin.
